topic.title: The UK energy price cap limits the rate you pay, not the size of your bill

title: The £1,723 energy price cap is not a limit on your bill
description: Ofgem's price cap is £1,723 a year for a typical household from October. But it caps the price per unit, not your total. A home that uses a quarter more energy pays more. Speak to a licensed financial adviser in your country before making financial decisions. Illustrative only. Not financial advice.

lines.text: The energy price cap means my bill is capped, right?
Ofgem's cap just went up £60, to £1,723 a year. But that is not a limit on your bill.
The cap limits the price of each unit of energy, and the daily standing charge.
That headline figure is just for a typical home, using a typical amount of energy.
Use more, in a cold home or working from home, and your bill could be 25% higher: £2,154.
That is £431 extra a year, at the very same capped prices.
The cap fixes the price. Your usage sets the bill.
Now you know what the cap really caps.
